HDFC Mutual Fund Help & FAQs - Statements & Reports HDFC Mutual Fund Help Center How do I download my Account Statement? You can download your account statement by following these steps: Go to the official HDFC Mutual Fund Investor Portal (https://www.hdfcfund.com). Log in using your PAN/Email/Folio Number and OTP/Password. Navigate to 'My Portfolio' and select 'Account Statements'. Choose the specific Folio Number and financial period. Click 'Download PDF' or select 'Request via Email' to receive it on your registered email address. Alternatively, you can request an account statement via SMS by sending 'HDFCMF STMT ' to 9212900022. How do I download my Capital Gains Report?

Alternatively, you can request an account statement via SMS by sending 'HDFCMF STMT ' to 9212900022. How do I download my Capital Gains Report? To download your Capital Gains statement for tax filing purposes, follow these steps: Visit the HDFC Mutual Fund customer portal. Click on 'Transact Online' or log in to your account. Select 'Statements' from the side menu, then click on 'Capital Gains Statement'. Select the relevant Financial Year (e.g., FY 2025-26). Click on 'Generate Report' and download the statement in PDF or Excel format. You can also download consolidated capital gains reports across multiple AMCs via the CAMS or KFintech registrar websites using your registered PAN. Last updated from sources: June 01, 2026.

AMFI Mutual Fund Investor Guidance & Resources Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) Investor Education & Awareness What is a Mutual Fund? A mutual fund is a pool of money managed by a professional fund manager. It trustfully invests the collected money in securities like stocks, bonds, and other short-term debt instruments. The combined holdings of the mutual fund are known as its portfolio. Each unit represents an investor's proportionate ownership of the portfolio's holdings and the income those holdings generate. Direct Plan vs. Regular Plan Mutual funds offer two plans: Direct and Regular. In a Direct Plan, an investor buys units directly from the Mutual Fund Company (AMC) without any intermediary, resulting in a lower expense ratio because no distributor commission is paid.

In a Regular Plan, units are bought through a broker, distributor, or agent, leading to a higher expense ratio because of agent commissions. Understanding Mutual Fund Riskometers SEBI mandates a riskometer to depict the risk level of mutual fund schemes. The six levels of risk are: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, and Very High. Investors should review the riskometer to align the scheme's risk level with their personal risk tolerance. Last updated from sources: June 01, 2026.
